hook.situation: A friend calls, the topic shifts to that friend, then the speaker contrasts messages with calls and answers who acted first. This chapter is about how Korean particles manage the flow of information.
objectives: Use 이/가 for new information, focused answers, and existence predicates.
Use 은/는 for topic continuity, contrast, and framing.
Build topic-plus-subject sentences such as 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.
hook.whyItMatters: English often uses word order or stress for information flow. Korean marks that flow with particles. 친구가 전화했어요 and 친구는 전화했어요 do not simply mean the same thing with different decoration.

grammarNotes.title: 이/가: new or focused subject
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 이/가 when the noun is the answer to "who/what?" or when it enters the conversation as the important subject.
grammarNotes.formation: Consonant-ending noun + 이, vowel-ending noun + 가. 저 becomes 제가.

examples.note: The sentence introduces who called, so 친구가 is new information.

examples.ko: 누가 먼저 연락했어요? 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
examples.romanization: nuga meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo? jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
examples.en: Who contacted them first? I contacted them first.
examples.note: 제가 answers the who-question and excludes other possible people.
있다/없다 normally takes 이/가 for the thing that exists.

exceptions: 이/가 is not only beginner subject marking. At B2, it often means focus or identification.
With 있다/없다, 이/가 is strongly preferred even if the noun is already understood.

grammarNotes.title: 은/는: topic continuity
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 은/는 when the noun is already on the table and you are now saying something about it.
grammarNotes.formation: Consonant-ending noun + 은, vowel-ending noun + 는. 그 친구는 means "as for that friend."

examples.note: The friend was already introduced with 친구가, so now 은/는 continues the topic.

examples.en: For this issue, the reason is the most important thing.
examples.note: 이 문제는 sets the frame; 이유가 is the important subject inside the frame.

examples.en: As for me, I understood the question.
examples.note: 저는 frames the speaker; 질문은 can mark the question as the limited topic.

exceptions: A noun can be old information but still take 이/가 if the sentence asks or answers "which one?"
은/는 can sound contrastive even when you did not intend contrast.

grammarNotes.title: 은/는: contrast and limited scope
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 은/는 when you compare one item with another or limit the statement to one area.
grammarNotes.formation: Put 은/는 on each compared item when you want the contrast to be visible.

examples.ko: 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
examples.romanization: pyeongsoeneun mesijireul bonaeneunde oneureun jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
examples.en: Usually they send messages, but today I contacted them first.
examples.note: 평소에는 and 오늘은 contrast usual days with today.

examples.ko: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
examples.romanization: mesijineun jaju bonaejiman jeonhwaneun jal an haeyo.
examples.en: I send messages often, but I do not call much.
examples.note: 메시지는 and 전화는 contrast two communication methods.

examples.en: The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
examples.note: 질문은 sets a contrastive topic; 대답이 introduces the part that was difficult.

exceptions: If you only want to say a new fact without contrast, 이/가 may be better.
Too many 은/는 markers can make every noun sound contrasted.

grammarNotes.title: 이/가: exactly this one
grammarNotes.mentalModel: When Korean answers "who?" or "what exactly?", 이/가 often means "this one, not the others."
grammarNotes.formation: Use 이/가 on the focused answer: 제가, 민수가, 이 문제가, 이유가.

examples.ko: 누가 먼저 연락했어요? 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
examples.romanization: nuga meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo? jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
examples.en: Who contacted them first? I did.

examples.ko: 무엇이 제일 중요해요? 이유가 제일 중요해요.
examples.romanization: mueosi jeil jungyohaeyo? iyuga jeil jungyohaeyo.
examples.en: What is most important? The reason is most important.
It is not the problem; the situation changed.
examples.note: 이/가 can sharpen the corrected focus.

exceptions: Do not translate this as an English article rule. The choice is about information focus, not a/an vs the.
저는 했어요 can sound like "as for me, I did it" and may imply contrast with others.

grammarNotes.title: Topic plus subject: N은/는 ... N이/가
grammarNotes.mentalModel: The topic sets the frame; 이/가 introduces the new or important subject inside that frame.
grammarNotes.formation: Topic noun + 은/는, then focused subject + 이/가: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.

examples.en: For this issue, the reason is the most important thing.
examples.note: The issue is the frame; the reason is the important subject.

examples.en: As for my opinion, the thinking is a little different.
examples.note: The topic narrows the area; 생각이 states what differs.

examples.ko: 한국어는 문장이 길어지면 조사가 더 중요해져요.
examples.romanization: hangugeoneun munjangi gireojimyeon josaga deo jungyohaejyeoyo.
examples.en: As for Korean, when sentences get longer, particles become more important.
examples.note: 한국어는 frames the subject area; 문장이 and 조사가 introduce local subjects.

exceptions: This double structure is not a mistake. It is a normal Korean discourse pattern.
Avoid forcing 은/는 onto every subject. The inner new subject still often needs 이/가.

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 전화했어요. 그 친구는 자주 전화하지 않아요.
exampleSentence.en: A friend called. That friend does not call often.
exampleSentence.note: First mention uses 가; continued topic uses 는.

exampleSentence.ko: 메시지는 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I send messages, but I do not call much.
exampleSentence.note: 전화는 contrasts calls with messages.

exampleSentence.ko: 누가 먼저 연락했어요? 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
exampleSentence.en: Who contacted first? I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 제가 answers 누가 with focus.

exampleSentence.ko: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I send messages often, but I do not call much.
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 makes the contrast visible.

exampleSentence.en: A text came, but no phone call came.
exampleSentence.note: 문자는 and 전화는 contrast two channels.

exampleSentence.en: Who contacted first?
exampleSentence.note: 누구 + 가 contracts to 누가.

exampleSentence.en: Today, I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 오늘은 contrasts today; 제가 identifies the actor.

exampleSentence.en: Does that friend call often?
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 keeps the friend as the topic while asking about habit.

exampleSentence.en: Usually they send messages, but today they called.
exampleSentence.note: 평소에는 contrasts the usual pattern with today.

exampleSentence.en: Today, I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 오늘은 contrasts today with other days.

exampleSentence.ko: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
exampleSentence.en: I send messages often, but I do not call much.
exampleSentence.note: The object 메시지 takes 를; the contrast uses 는.

exampleSentence.en: The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
exampleSentence.note: 질문은 is the contrastive topic.

exampleSentence.en: The answer was difficult.
exampleSentence.note: 대답이 introduces the part that was difficult.

exampleSentence.en: As for my opinion, the thinking is a little different.
exampleSentence.note: 의견은 frames the topic; 생각이 states what differs.

exampleSentence.en: That idea is good, but the reason is lacking.
exampleSentence.note: 생각은 frames the idea; 이유가 introduces the problem.

exampleSentence.en: For this issue, the reason is the most important thing.
exampleSentence.note: 문제는 sets the frame; 이유가 is the key subject.

exampleSentence.en: What is important? The reason is important.
exampleSentence.note: 이유가 answers 무엇이.

exampleSentence.en: The two expressions have a difference.
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 frames the two expressions; 차이가 states what exists.

exampleSentence.ko: 이런 상황에서는 제가 먼저 말해야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: In this kind of situation, I should speak first.
exampleSentence.note: 상황에서는 frames the condition; 제가 identifies the actor.

exampleSentence.en: The truth is, I contacted first.
exampleSentence.note: 사실은 frames the correction.

exampleSentence.en: As for the two people, their opinions are different.
exampleSentence.note: 두 사람은 is the frame; 의견이 is the differing subject.

exampleSentence.en: The meaning is the same, but the feeling is different.
exampleSentence.note: 은/는 contrasts meaning and feeling.

exampleSentence.en: The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
exampleSentence.note: 쉬웠는데 sets up contrast.

exampleSentence.en: For this issue, the reason is most important.
exampleSentence.note: 중요하다 often appears with the focused subject marked by 이/가.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two friends analyze a call and a message while the particles track new information, topic, contrast, and focus.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.grammarNote: 친구가 introduces the caller as new information.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.grammarNote: The friend is now the topic, so 그 친구는 is natural.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 아니요. 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
lines.romanization: aniyo. pyeongsoeneun mesijireul bonaeneunde oneureun jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
lines.en: No. Usually they send messages, but today I contacted them first.
lines.grammarNote: 평소에는 and 오늘은 contrast time frames; 제가 focuses the actor.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.grammarNote: 누가 asks for the focused subject.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 제가 먼저 연락했어요. 질문은 쉬웠는데 대답이 어려웠어요.
lines.romanization: jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo. jilmuneun swiwonneunde daedabi eoryeowosseoyo.
lines.en: I contacted first. The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.
lines.grammarNote: 제가 answers who; 질문은 contrasts with 대답이.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그럼 이 문제는 이유가 제일 중요하네요.
lines.romanization: geureom i munjeneun iyuga jeil jungyohaneyo.
lines.en: Then for this issue, the reason is the most important thing.
lines.grammarNote: 이 문제는 frames the topic; 이유가 is the important subject.

readingText.title: 친구가에서 그 친구는으로
readingText.body: 어제 민서에게 친구가 전화했다. 처음 말할 때는 누가 전화했는지가 새 정보였기 때문에 친구가 자연스러웠다. 그다음 지훈은 "그 친구는 자주 전화해?"라고 물었다. 이미 말한 친구를 다시 주제로 삼았기 때문에 그 친구는이 맞았다. 민서는 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했다고 설명했다. 여기서 평소에는과 오늘은은 서로 대비된다. 지훈이 "누가 먼저 연락했어?"라고 묻자 민서는 "제가 먼저 연락했어"라고 답했다. 제가는 다른 사람이 아니라 바로 민서가 했다는 뜻이다. 마지막으로 "이 문제는 이유가 중요해"처럼 말하면, 문제는 이야기의 틀이고 이유가 그 안에서 중요한 새 정보가 된다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Yesterday, a friend called Minseo. On the first mention, who called was new information, so 친구가 was natural. Then Jihoon asked, "Does that friend call often?" Because the friend had already been mentioned and was now the topic, 그 친구는 was right. Minseo explained that usually the friend sends messages, but today she contacted first. Here 평소에는 and 오늘은 contrast with each other. When Jihoon asked, "Who contacted first?" Minseo answered, "I contacted first." 제가 means it was specifically Minseo, not someone else. Finally, in a sentence like "For this issue, the reason is important," 문제는 is the frame of the discussion and 이유가 is the important new information inside it.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요에서 문제와 이유의 역할은 무엇이에요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 문제는 이야기의 틀이고, 이유가 그 안에서 중요한 새 정보예요.

culturalNote.title: 조사는 대화의 카메라다
culturalNote.body: Korean particles move the camera of the conversation. 이/가 zooms in on the subject that matters now. 은/는 sets the frame or contrasts one frame with another. This is why native speakers can hear a difference between 제가 했어요 and 저는 했어요 even when both contain I. 제가 answers who did it. 저는 often sounds like as for me, possibly contrasting with someone else.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing a particle, ask whether the noun is the new answer, the continuing topic, or one side of a contrast.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence introduces the caller as new information?
Which sentence contrasts messages and calls?
options: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
메시지가 자주 보내지만 전화가 잘 안 해요.
메시지에게 자주 보내지만 전화에게 안 해요.
inlineExercises.correct: 메시지는 자주 보내지만 전화는 잘 안 해요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 은/는 marks the two contrasted communication methods.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which answer fits 누가 먼저 연락했어요?
Which particles complete the topic-plus-subject sentence: 이 문제____ 이유____ 중요해요?
inlineExercises.explanation: 이 문제는 sets the frame; 이유가 is the important subject inside it.

bullets: 이/가 introduces or focuses the subject: 친구가 전화했어요, 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
은/는 continues or frames the topic: 그 친구는 자주 전화해요?, 이 문제는...
은/는 also marks contrast: 평소에는..., 오늘은..., 메시지는..., 전화는...
A Korean sentence can have both: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.
